title: Astrid and the Hollow
premise: Kestrel Eastwick has survived ten years in the magic-outlawed city of Vell by being small: a royal food-taster, a discreet charm-seller, a woman no one remembers twice. But when her new lover, the cartographer Ilan Voss, appears in a century-old book of prophecies as 'the Hollow Man who opens the door,' Kestrel realizes the charms she's been selling were never harmless—they've been quietly feeding a sealed entity beneath the palace called the Hollow. The prophecy names a second figure, 'the Taster of Deaths,' and Kestrel understands she was bred for this role by the very order that outlawed magic to monopolize it. As the Hollow's influence spreads through the court—corrupting the young queen she serves—Kestrel must choose between loyalty to the crown that raised her and the truth that her immunity was built from stolen deaths. In the end, Kestrel swallows the Hollow itself, using her trained body as its prison, becoming both its keeper and its hostage; Ilan, revealed as the prophecy's unwitting key, seals the door behind her, and Kestrel rules nothing but the dark room where she waits.
about_author: Petra Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent seven years cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people whose small, practical magics go unnoticed until they become dangerous.

chapters.title: The Ninth Dish
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. During a state dinner, Kestrel tastes nine courses without flinching, hiding the numbness spreading across her tongue—a side effect of ten years of controlled poisoning. She notices Ilan Voss sketching her from across the hall. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional composure; something is changing in her body.

chapters.title: Charms for Small Coin
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In the night market, Kestrel sells minor charms—luck knots, fever wards—while dodging the Wardens who enforce the magic ban. A customer pays with an old coin stamped with a spiral sigil she's seen only once before, on the palace's foundation stone. Emotional beat: the thrill and fragility of her double life.

chapters.title: A Man Drawn Twice
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV. Ilan, a court cartographer, maps not land but patterns—he's traced a spiral recurring across Vell's oldest buildings. He approaches Kestrel at the market, drawn by a face he's sketched repeatedly in dreams he's never told anyone about. Emotional beat: magnetic recognition shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: The Book Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Cleaning the taster's quarters, Kestrel finds a hidden cache: a prophecy book written a century ago, its pages describing tonight's date, a man with Ilan's exact face, and 'the Taster of Deaths.' The final page is torn out. Emotional beat: vertigo—the life she built was scripted before she was born.

chapters.title: What the Queen Doesn't Know
chapters.summary: Queen Maren's POV. The nineteen-year-old queen privately practices small forbidden cantrips, taught by her late mother, unaware that each spell drains into the palace foundations. She trusts Kestrel completely—and asks her to taste an unmarked gift from a foreign envoy. Emotional beat: loneliness at the top, and the first seed of corruption.

chapters.title: The Envoy's Gift
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The gift is honey wine; Kestrel tastes it and tastes nothing—which should be impossible, since it's laced with a poison that kills in minutes. She survives because her immunity absorbs it, but the spiral sigil on the bottle confirms someone knows what she is. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Order of the Sealed Table
chapters.summary: Master Corvane's POV. The head of the Tasters' Guild reveals to his inner circle that the guild founded the magic ban, that the Hollow beneath the palace is real, and that it must be fed—or it will wake. He orders surveillance on Kestrel, whose bloodline was engineered for a purpose he resents. Emotional beat: cold institutional ruthlessness masking fear.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel confronts Corvane, who admits her childhood 'adoption' was breeding-program selection: every dish she tasted fed the Hollow through her blood. Her immunity isn't protection—it's cultivation. Emotional beat: betrayal collapsing her identity; rage finding focus.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV. Ilan tells Kestrel about his dreams and shows her his spiral map: the pattern converges beneath the throne room. He believes he's meant to open something, and he's terrified—but more afraid of what happens if he refuses. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared doom; love declared honestly.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Wardens raid Kestrel's charm stall—not for her crimes, but to seize her, ordered by someone inside the palace who wants the Taster of Deaths contained. She escapes through the night market using a charm she never sold: one that erases memory. Emotional beat: hunted; the cost of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Queen's Hunger
chapters.summary: Queen Maren's POV. Maren's cantrips grow effortless and vast; she levitates the court chandelier to applause and doesn't remember doing it. She begins hearing a voice from below calling her 'the open hand.' Emotional beat: intoxication curdling into possession—the theme of power's corruption embodied.

chapters.title: Below the Foundations
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Ilan's alternating POV. Following the spiral map through forgotten servant tunnels, they reach a sealed door older than the city, warm to the touch. Through it, Kestrel hears her own name spoken in her dead mother's voice. Emotional beat: awe and horror; the past is not past.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel recovers the missing prophecy page from Corvane's safe: it names the ending—'the Taster swallows the dark, and the dark learns her name.' It also reveals the Hollow was once a person: the first queen, consumed by her own magic. Emotional beat: grief reframing the enemy; the monster has a history.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane offers Kestrel a deal: surrender herself to the guild's ritual, which will transfer the Hollow into a condemned prisoner instead, sparing her but damning an innocent. He genuinely believes this is mercy. Emotional beat: the seductive logic of institutional evil; loyalty vs. truth crystallized.

chapters.title: What Ilan Saw
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV. Ilan secretly meets a Warden defector who shows him records proving the prophecy book was written by the first queen herself—a warning sent backward, or a trap laid forward; even the defector can't tell which. Ilan realizes opening the door may be the only way to close it. Emotional beat: resolve hardening; accepting complicity.

chapters.title: The Feast of Ashes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At the coronation-anniversary feast, the Hollow rises through Maren, who publicly performs miracles while her eyes go spiral-black. Corvane's guild moves to seize her; the Wardens turn on everyone. Kestrel tastes the air and tastes death everywhere. Emotional beat: chaos, spectacle, the mask of the court shattering.

chapters.title: The Door Opens
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV. Guided by the prophecy and his own dreams, Ilan unseals the ancient door beneath the throne room. What emerges isn't a monster but a vast absence wearing the first queen's shape, offering each person present exactly what they most want. Emotional beat: temptation as apocalypse; desire weaponized.

chapters.title: Swallowing the Dark
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel refuses the Hollow's offer—her mother, alive again—and instead does what ten years of training prepared her for: she takes it in, tasting it fully, letting her cultivated body become its cage. Agony, then stillness. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax; the taster finally consumes the poison whole.

chapters.title: The Sealing
chapters.summary: Ilan's POV. With the Hollow bound inside Kestrel, Ilan redraws the spiral with himself as its center, closing the door forever and severing the prophecy's loop—he will never dream again, and forgets her face as the price. Emotional beat: bittersweet sacrifice; love paying truth's toll.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Miracles
chapters.summary: Queen Maren's POV. Freed from the Hollow, Maren must reckon publicly with what she did, choosing abdication of her magical claims rather than her crown, and abolishing the Tasters' Guild. She spares Kestrel's life against all counsel. Emotional beat: chastened power; redemption earned through accountability.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Room
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel lives now in a warded chamber beneath the rebuilt palace, visited by Maren, sustained by ordinary meals she can barely taste. The Hollow speaks to her sometimes; she answers with silence. Emotional beat: quiet, costly peace—power contained by choice, not law.

chapters.title: A Charm for Remembering
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Years later, a young archivist brings Kestrel a recovered sketchbook: Ilan's drawings, including her face, drawn over and over by a man who couldn't remember why. Kestrel smiles, presses the page to her chest, and begins teaching the girl a charm—one small, honest magic. Emotional beat: hope persisting in captivity; legacy as quiet resistance.
